div.head: Iud Dei XII 1
div.ab: Romani propter thesaurum Sancti Petri et inuidiam simul tulerunt Leoni papę oculos et linguam olim.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 420 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Leo III. wurde durch Verschworene zu Rom am 25. April 799 misshandelt. Zeitgenossen berichten als Grund invidia, und Plünderung, aber nicht Wegnahme des Schatzes Petri. Dass Leo Zunge und Augen verlor, übertrieben schon Zeitgenossen. Er traf im Juli Karl zu Paderborn; dieser liess ihn im November in Rom restituieren, kam selbst erst ein Jahr später dorthin, verhandelte im Dezember 800 gegen Leos Feinde, ohne dass vom Schatze oder einem Ordal die Rede wäre; Simson Karl d. Gr. II 163 ff. 179. 242. 583

Leo III was maltreated by conspirators at Rome on 25 April 799. Contemporaries report invidia as the reason, and plundering, but not the removal of St Peter’s treasure. That Leo lost his tongue and eyes was an exaggeration even among contemporaries. In July he met Charles at Paderborn; Charles had him restored at Rome in November, but himself came there only a year later, and in December 800 conducted proceedings against Leo’s enemies, without any mention of the treasure or of an ordeal; Simson Karl d. Gr. II 163 ff. 179. 242. 583

div.ab: The Romans, on account of the treasure of St Peter and out of envy, once took away from Pope Leo both his eyes and his tongue.
